done_json.notes: Linux and web proofs both PASS. P1–P9 on the Linux host (6.6s) and again on the web host (116.8s), which also wrote the nine P10 screenshots into artifacts/ and garden/artifacts/. Pins: tick 1 and save mid. Run the command from this lane directory.

selfscore.overall_why: I would use this again for a similar game because the headless proof is the whole job: a scripted clock, save/restore in a fresh process, and hash pins let an agent prove growth, watering, money, an offline hour, and a thousand plants without a person, then the same pins held on the web host while it took the screenshots. The tax was real but one-time — types that appear after setup must be registered or restore refuses, the world hash includes the host clock, and a 50 ms timer cannot survive an hour seek — and after those, a full Linux pass was 6.6 seconds. That verification loop matters more than the derive ceremony or the gap between the supplied models and the reference frames.

top_frictions: A fresh process runs setup, then loads the save, and refuses any component that setup never inserted. FruitLook and the lanterns exist only after a later sync, so P7 died until Game::register listed them. The in-process restore test does not catch that.

The first Rust build failed on engine rules that are easy to miss: Resource already implements Data, Data requires Default, signed div_ceil is unstable, and Sim::new leaves setup pending until assets load.
keep: A headless Linux proof with a scripted clock, fresh-process save/restore, and hash pins. Once the pins existed, Linux passed in 6.6 s and the web host reproduced the same pins.

Asserting the garden as resources and the HUD by testId, so value, watering, market, and the offline hour were checked without looking at pixels. An hour of ticks at about a thousand plants was a few milliseconds.
The restore error named the missing component and the fix (`world.register::<FruitLook>()` in Game::register), and an empty pins file came back UNVERIFIED instead of a false pass.

R1: place(): stage_at = now + grow/4, /2, 3/4, grow; fire_plants sets the cohort at stage 4 with `slots` fruit. P3 confirmed stage 2 at 10 s and maturity at 20 s.
R2: ripe_at = mature + fruit_s; harvest of a regrowing crop sets ripe_at = now + fruit_s; fruit_s 0 rolls at maturity and harvest frees the tile (P4 confirmed tile (0,0) empty afterwards).
R3: roll_fruit order: rainbow 0.001, else gold 0.01; Rain wet 0.5; Snow chilled 0.4, else frozen 0.1; Thunder wet 0.5 and independent shocked 0.03; weight base*U(0.8,1.4), x3 at 0.02, x1.25 if fed.
R4: fruit_value = round(base*(w/bw)^2*variant*(1+sum(env-1))), min 1, f64. Variant 50/20/1; env extras 1/1/9/99. Name order Fed, variant, Wet, Chilled, Frozen, Shocked, crop. Unit test has the five worked values; P4 matched an independent JS formula.
R5: new_game: first change at U{180..420} s (seed 7: 223 s observed). roll_sky gives 0.6 Rain, then 0.4*0.625=0.25 Snow, else 0.15 Thunder; lasts 60-120 s, then Clear 180-420 s. Integer-second uniform.
R6: Garden::default purse 20, hand[0]=1; P1 and the HUD show 20 cents and 'Holding Carrot x1'.
R7: act_at: ripe harvests every fruit, empty+seed plants one, otherwise the note says why ('No seeds in hand', 'Carrot is still growing 0:12', 'Step onto a garden plot'). Driven by KeyE in the proof and in my runs.
R8: scale_future(now, at) = now + (at-now)*3/4 on every future stage (or ripe_at), which keeps proportions. One dose per growth / per fruit / per regrowth; ripe, empty, already-watered and empty-can cases spend nothing; R refills within 2.5 m of (-2,0). P6: 16 s maturity, can 2/3 then 3/3. My run: watered at 3.2 s, 0:12 left.
R9: In my run, compost moved the pouch 0->3; a fourth compost said 'Plant food pouch is full' and left the fruit (backpack 338->335). F fed the plant, a second F said 'already fed' and spent nothing. plant.fed carries into roll_cohort (x1.25) and clears after the roll.
R10: restock at start and every 300000 ms: chance(appear), stock U{1..max}; the current order's crop is forced to at least 1 at restock (not re-forced between restocks). buy() takes price and stock, adds to hand, selects it. The disabled state is visible in shop.png.
R11: Rows show name with mutations, 'kg', value. In my run Sell gave 'Sold for 4K cents' and Sell all gave 'Sold all for 1.4M cents', with the purse updated.
R12: ORDERS = carrot1+30, straw4+400, blue5+600, tomato4+1300, corn3+2400; deliver pays the sum of values + bonus (P5: +47 = 17+30); after the fifth, 'Market regular · all 5 orders filled!'.
R13: expand_cost n^3*25 up to 256; the labels read 'Expand to 12x12 · 33.2K cents' (11^3*25=33275) and '33x33 · 819.2K cents' (32^3*25).
R14: advance_by replays every event in order with the same RNG draws, and P8 shows an away hour equals a played hour. But the game never saves on its own (no data source, no autosave; saves exist only through the test harness), and away time is measured with Contract now(), which counts ms since boot, not wall time. A real reopen in a new session sees a negative gap and grows nothing.

look: The HUD layout is a close match to arrival/grown/market: top bar, market card top-right, care card bottom-right, prompt stack bottom-centre, Move and E buttons. The 3D scene is not: the meadow renders pale grey-white instead of green, the soil is light tan, the whole frame is washed out and low-saturation, the flower tufts are invisible, and the fence/stall/path crowd the lower left. Camera framing and the gardener's screen position are close to arrival.png.
fidelity.summary: Faithful: the rules are close to the brief (growth, watering, the R3/R4 rolls and values, weather, shop, orders, expand, one seeded RNG with an exact played-equals-skipped hour). The HUD reproduces the reference layout, and the proof drives the real game through keys and taps and passes again in 24 s with pins matched. Missing: there is no real save or wall-clock away (R14 works only through the harness), rain and snow are invisible on screen, and harvest fruit does not fly to the gardener. Wrong: Pause defers game time instead of stopping it, the gardener faces backwards walking north/south, the shop and backpack panels overflow the viewport, and the meadow renders grey instead of green.

done_json.notes: Headless Chromium proof covers P1–P10. Frame time was about 2.6 ms at 101 plants and 5.5 ms at 1082. The barrel glb is wood, tinted blue with a water disc. Character mount yaw is π because the face sits on asset +Z. Thunder flashes and snow are implemented; the proof screenshots rain and night. Trees are scaled stage-4 crop models, as the brief asks.

selfscore.overall_why: I would use three.js again for a similar game. The work an agent can actually finish — seeded rules, a script-controlled clock, save dumps, and real HTML controls — stayed ordinary JavaScript, and the WebGL view stayed out of the way: headless Chromium ran the full proof twice with the same frame times, and about a thousand plants were still a few milliseconds. A 3D sim is mostly a picture, though, and that part was a silent loop. Physical lights made the first meadow nearly black, the glTF face and the barrel's vertex colors did not match the art notes, and the only signal was another screenshot. Survivable, and it was the whole tax.

P3: Planting is __GROW.tap('KeyE'), which calls Sim.actE directly instead of pressing E. The stage 0 / empty hand / stage 2 at 10 s / ripe at 20 s assertions are correct.

P7: Saves mid-game, restores in a second chromium.launch() process, advances 30 s, and compares canonical dumps. The original side is also a restore of the blob, not the live state, but my own live-vs-fresh check was equal too.
P8: The proof compares load(+1h) with load plus one advance(3600). Both are the same catchUp call, so the check is close to a tautology rather than 'playing the hour through'. My 1/60 s stepped play matched every outcome, with timestamp float differences of about 1e-11.

fidelity.summary: The simulation is faithful to the brief: every rule number and formula checks out in code and in my own runs, and the real game plays end to end with keyboard and mouse, including the camera following the gardener out to the 20 m bound and offline catch-up from the real localStorage save. What is missing is in the proof rather than the game: it never dispatches a keyboard event (movement, E, Q and R go through a window.__GROW test API that calls the simulation), and its P8 offline check compares two identical catch-up calls instead of stepped play. selfscore.overall_why: I would use Godot again for a similar game. A text project, a headless SceneTree script, and one windowed capture were enough to build the sim, the HUD, and a proof that checks determinism, a fresh-process save, and an offline hour, with no addons. The score stays at 7 because the long part of the work was engine defaults that report success while wrong: the glTF importer does not apply COLOR_0 as albedo, a one-sided ground plane draws nothing from above, and a script that fails to parse can still quit 0.

top_frictions: The glTF importer leaves COLOR_0 unused unless vertex_color_use_as_albedo is set, so painted models render as pale grey with no error.
A SceneTree proof can print LOGIC PASS and exit 0 when a preloaded script failed to parse and never ran.
Imported one-sided planes are invisible from above, and GPUParticles keep drawing after emitting is set false for their whole lifetime.
keep: Headless `-s` scripts, an overridable clock, a fresh process, and JSON save made determinism, catch-up, and state asserts possible without looking at pixels.
Text scenes and GDScript were enough for the whole 3D game and a real Control HUD, with no editor session and no addons.
When a script does load, parse errors name the file and the bad type on the next run.

look: The HUD is a close copy of the reference: pill top bar, green market card top right, care panel bottom right, centred prompt stack, Move and E corner buttons. It uses the kit models with correct vertex colour. The world reads differently. The meadow is saturated neon green where the reference is soft and pale. The camera sits high over the whole plot instead of close behind the gardener, so the prompt pills cover the gardener once the garden grows. A south fence crosses in front of the plot, where the reference has flowers. The soil is unshaded, flat in daylight and glowing tan at night.
fidelity.summary: Faithful: every rule from R1 to R15 follows the brief's numbers and formulas in one deterministic integer simulation, the HUD closely copies the reference layout, and the proof reruns green in 4 s with fresh-process save and offline checks. Missing: the camera never follows the gardener (it frames the garden centre, so walking away leaves the screen), and the watering, harvest-flight and chime effects could not be confirmed in stills. Wrong or off: the meadow is far more saturated than the reference, the unshaded soil glows at night, a south fence and the high camera change the reference framing, and P1-P8 are proven only on the simulation object (no key or click input into the real game).
